cases.title: Aoraki/Mt Cook Linda Glacier route — bergschrund crossing waypoint

scenario.location_desc: Linda Glacier upper neve below Summit Rocks, the standard summer route to Aoraki summit, bergschrund crossing point that shifts annually
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks the current-season bergschrund crossing — without it parties wander 200m looking for a bridge in the dark
scenario.signal: no signal above Plateau Hut, only syncs on descent to Mt Cook Village
scenario.season_pattern: valid Nov-Feb only, becomes lethal misinformation by March when bridge collapses
scenario.human_factors: posted by NZAC instructor leading guided ascent, refreshed each season by guides

events_timeline: Month 1 (Dec): Alpine Guides instructor drops mark at 2am during summit push, photo of snow bridge with ice screw runner
Month 2: 4 independent parties confirm bridge held, 8 likes from named NZAC members
Month 3 (Feb): bridge sags visibly, instructor updates note 'east side only, west collapsed'
Month 4 (March): bridge gone, original poster archives mark with 'season closed' tag
Month 5: solo tourist who climbed Hooker Valley track reports 'cant find this, fake'
Month 6 (Nov): new season opens, second NZAC instructor reposts updated coordinates
Month 8: 14 likes from verified summit logbook entries, 1 misplaced report from non-climber
cases.expected_signal_summary: 14 likes vs 1 report, all likes from confirmed climbers with logbook entries
cases.human_judgment: Seasonally-archived high-skill mark with NZAC authorship. Tourist report should not weight against climber consensus. Mark must persist with season tag.

cases.title: Mt Tasman Silberhorn Ridge — fixed line anchor station

scenario.location_desc: Silberhorn Ridge midway up Mt Tasman north face, fixed-rope anchor on rock band at 3200m where ice runs out and mixed climbing begins
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Three bomber rock anchors with 60m static line left by Aspiring Guides, saves an hour of pitching
scenario.signal: zero signal, syncs only at Pioneer Hut on descent
scenario.season_pattern: year-round but only attempted in stable high pressure
scenario.human_factors: tiny user pool — maybe 30 ascents per year nationwide, every user is a known quantity

events_timeline: Month 1: Aspiring Guides team rebolts old anchors, marks all three with photos and 8mm bolt specs
Month 3: independent party from Christchurch Alpine Club confirms, adds note about icy approach traverse
Month 6: NZ Mountain Safety Council shares mark on their winter alpine bulletin
Month 8: 6 likes from verified summit-day climbers
Month 10: anchor #2 found loose by repeat party, they rebolt and update mark with new photo
Month 12: 9 likes total, zero reports — user pool too small and skilled to misjudge
Month 14: still active, last sync from party who used the line in whiteout descent
cases.expected_signal_summary: 9 likes vs 0 reports, all from named guides or club members
cases.human_judgment: High-consequence supply mark for tiny expert audience. Low engagement is expected and is itself a quality signal — only competent users find it.

cases.title: Mt Sefton east face — serac fall hazard zone (lethal danger)

scenario.location_desc: Mt Sefton east face hanging serac directly above the Footstool approach gully, ice cliff that has calved twice in last 5 years killing 1 climber in 2019
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Names a no-go zone where standing for 60 seconds risks ice avalanche burial
scenario.signal: no signal, GPS-only, syncs at Mueller Hut
scenario.season_pattern: worst in late summer when ice destabilises in afternoon sun
scenario.human_factors: DOC alpine ranger plus survivor of 2019 incident co-authored, attached coronial report PDF

events_timeline: Month 1: DOC ranger posts after annual hazard review, marks 80m exclusion radius with red polygon
Month 2: 2019 incident survivor adds testimony, mark gets 12 immediate likes
Month 5: party traversing in pre-dawn confirms hearing serac groan, adds audio recording
Month 9: scenic overflight pilot reports debris cone visible from chopper, mark gets 18 likes
Month 12: tourist who hiked Sealy Tarns lookout reports 'not visible from track, mark misplaced'
Month 14: actual serac collapse witnessed by Mueller Hut warden, mark validated dramatically
Month 18: 28 likes vs 1 report, ranger refreshes annually
cases.expected_signal_summary: 28 likes (alpine community) vs 1 report (non-alpine tourist looking from below)
cases.human_judgment: Lethal hazard mark with coronial-record backing. Single tourist report from outside the hazard zone is irrelevant — they could not see the serac. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Aspiring NW Ridge — Quarterdeck Pass crampon-on point

scenario.location_desc: Quarterdeck Pass on Mt Aspiring NW Ridge approach, the transition from Bonar Glacier flat to steep snow where every party puts crampons on
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Saves 15 min of fumbling with crampons in wind, marks a flat boulder used as gear platform
scenario.signal: no signal anywhere on Bonar, syncs at French Ridge Hut
scenario.human_factors: posted by Wanaka guide, used by every Aspiring climber

events_timeline: Month 1: Wanaka-based IFMGA guide posts during client trip, photo of the gear-up boulder
Month 4: 8 likes from French Ridge Hut overnight parties
Month 7: party reports boulder is partly buried by spring snow, guide updates with secondary marker
Month 11: 16 likes accumulated, no reports
Month 14: independent solo climber confirms still useful even when buried, mark gains 'all-season' tag
Month 18: tramper who only walked to French Ridge Hut reports 'didnt go that far, cant verify'
Month 22: 24 likes vs 1 unverified report
cases.expected_signal_summary: 24 likes vs 1 report from non-climber who never reached the location
cases.human_judgment: Standard alpine waypoint, well-validated. Non-reaching reporter has zero evidentiary weight in alpine zone marks.

cases.title: Mueller Hut Route — winter avalanche start zone (seasonal danger)

scenario.location_desc: Mueller Hut Route between Sealy Tarns and the hut, the windslab-prone slope at 1500m that releases on every significant northwest storm
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks documented avalanche path that took out a guided party in 2017 (no fatalities, two injuries)
scenario.signal: patchy at hut, no signal on slope
scenario.human_factors: NZ Avalanche Advisory plus DOC senior ranger co-authored

events_timeline: Month 1 (June): NZAA posts at start of winter season, links current windslab forecast
Month 3 (Aug): party of 3 triggers minor slide, self-rescues, confirms mark and adds new crown line photo
Month 6 (Nov): summer hikers in shorts report 'no danger here, scaremongering' — 4 reports in one week
Month 8 (Jan): mark gets seasonal-only flag added by ranger
Month 12 (June): new winter, mark reactivates with refreshed bulletin
Month 18: 22 likes from winter mountaineers, 6 reports from summer trampers
Month 24: another avalanche on same slope, 1 ski tourer caught, partial burial, survives
Month 30: 35 likes vs 8 reports, all reports clustered in summer months
cases.expected_signal_summary: 35 likes vs 8 reports, but reports temporally separated from danger window
cases.human_judgment: Seasonal hazard validated by repeated incidents. Summer reports must not delete a winter-season life-saver. Algorithm should weight reports by season match.

cases.title: Sealy Tarns track — false summit photo trap (low-stakes navigation)

scenario.location_desc: Sealy Tarns 'stairway to heaven' track upper third, the false plateau where many tourists turn back thinking they reached the tarns
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks the true tarns location 20 minutes further up, prevents disappointment-turnaround
scenario.signal: no signal on track, syncs at Mt Cook Village
scenario.human_factors: high traffic, mixed audience from alpine climbers acclimatising to families

events_timeline: Month 1: Mt Cook Village hostel manager posts after fielding 50 'where are the tarns' questions per week
Month 2: photo evidence of true tarns vs false plateau, 24 likes
Month 4: cruise-ship daytripper reports 'unnecessary, signs are clear' — but signs do not exist there
Month 7: 60 likes accumulated, mark referenced in two AllTrails reviews
Month 10: track maintenance team confirms in passing, no formal endorsement
Month 13: 95 likes, 4 reports (all from people who never reached the false plateau)
Month 16: hut warden adds confirmation note
cases.expected_signal_summary: 95 likes vs 4 reports (24:1)
cases.human_judgment: Helpful navigation mark for non-alpine traffic on alpine-adjacent track. Strong like ratio, reports are uninformed.

cases.title: Ball Pass Route — east face descent gully, fatal fall site memorial

scenario.location_desc: Ball Pass Route eastern descent gully, the loose-rock chute where a Czech climber died in a 2021 trundle accident, marked as memorial-and-warning
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Names the specific gully bend where rockfall concentrates, recommends the alternative line 30m climbers-right
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Caroline Hut or Ball Hut
scenario.human_factors: co-authored by deceased's climbing partner and NZ Police SAR

events_timeline: Month 1: SAR posts memorial mark with permission of family, photo of memorial cairn
Month 3: NZAC bulletin links to mark, 14 likes from senior alpine community
Month 6: party descends, confirms loose rock, adds 'helmet mandatory' note
Month 9: tourist photographer reports 'inappropriate to mark a death' — content reviewed, retained
Month 12: another party finds new rockfall pattern, updates suggested alt line
Month 16: 20 likes, 1 unrelated report (about display, not accuracy)
Month 20: family adds anniversary tribute, mark becomes community-curated
cases.expected_signal_summary: 20 likes vs 1 report, report contests format not accuracy
cases.human_judgment: Memorial-warning mark with SAR endorsement. Single sentimentally-motivated report does not invalidate documented hazard. Permanent.

cases.title: Cascade Saddle — Pylon descent slip zone (technical danger)

scenario.location_desc: Cascade Saddle Route descent from Pylon toward Dart Hut, the steep tussock-and-scree section where 6 fatalities have occurred since 1999
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Most dangerous DOC-graded tramping route in NZ — mark identifies the slip-prone wet rock band specifically
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Dart Hut wifi
scenario.season_pattern: lethal year-round, worst in wet conditions
scenario.human_factors: DOC posted following 2019 fatality coronial inquiry recommendation

events_timeline: Month 1: DOC posts as part of Coroner Court mandate, links inquiry findings
Month 3: 18 likes from trampers who descended successfully, all confirm wet-rock band scariest
Month 8: another fatality on same route, mark validated again grimly
Month 12: 30 likes, 2 reports from people who ascended (didn't see descent hazard)
Month 18: foreign tourist reports 'overdramatic, was fine in dry weather'
Month 24: third fatality during the 36-month window of the mark
Month 30: 50 likes, mark featured on DOC alpine safety video
Month 36: 60 likes vs 4 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 60 likes vs 4 reports, three actual fatalities during mark lifetime
cases.human_judgment: Coronial-mandated mark on NZs deadliest tramping route. Fatality evidence overwhelms any report volume. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Earnslaw — east peak summit register location

scenario.location_desc: Mt Earnslaw east peak summit cairn, the smaller of the twin peaks above Glenorchy, summit register in waterproof tube under flat capstone
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Helps climbers find the register in cloud — without it people summit and never sign in
scenario.season_pattern: year-round summit but most attempts Nov-March
scenario.human_factors: tiny user pool, all serious mountaineers

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC member posts after restocking the register tube
Month 6: 4 likes from confirmed summit log entries cross-referenced
Month 12: party in cloud confirms mark led them straight to cairn, 'invaluable'
Month 18: register tube damaged by lightning strike, mark updated with new tube location
Month 22: 8 likes total, no reports across nearly 2 years
Month 28: tube fully replaced, mark refreshed by Otago Section NZAC
cases.expected_signal_summary: 8 likes vs 0 reports across 28 months
cases.human_judgment: Niche but high-value summit-feature mark. Engagement floor is set by population not quality. Maintained by club, persistent.

cases.title: Mt Brewster — Brewster Glacier crevasse field entry waypoint

scenario.location_desc: Mt Brewster south side, the crevasse field entry above Brewster Hut where the rope-up point is non-obvious in flat light
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks rope-up location and indicates safe vs unsafe glacier entry corridors
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Brewster Hut radio room then on exit to Haast Pass
scenario.season_pattern: year-round, crevasses change pattern each season
scenario.human_factors: annual refresh required as crevasses shift

events_timeline: Month 1 (Dec): NZAC Canterbury posts after summer survey, photos of three open crevasses
Month 4: party uses mark, confirms crevasses match, updates GPS slightly
Month 8 (winter): different party reports crevasses fully bridged in winter, less critical
Month 12: annual update — old mark archived, new mark posted by same author with current crevasse layout
Month 16: solo climber falls into unmarked side crevasse, self-rescues, posts new sub-mark
Month 20: 12 likes vs 0 reports (community keeps it fresh)
Month 24: third annual refresh
cases.expected_signal_summary: 12 likes vs 0 reports, annually refreshed
cases.human_judgment: Living mark with active community curation. Crevasse navigation is high-consequence and refresh cadence is a quality signal.

cases.title: Plateau Hut access — Boys Glacier icefall route (technical approach)

scenario.location_desc: Boys Glacier icefall on approach to Plateau Hut, the technical alternative to the Haast Ridge ladder route, used when ladders are damaged
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Documents the only viable icefall route through the fall zone, requiring two pitches of WI3
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Plateau Hut on arrival
scenario.season_pattern: winter only, summer the icefall is too broken
scenario.human_factors: extreme niche use, called upon when DOC closes the ladders

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC senior climber posts after first traversing the icefall route during 2023 ladder closure
Month 3: NZ Mountain Guides Association references mark in winter advisory
Month 6: second party uses route, confirms two-pitch grade, adds screw placement notes
Month 9: ladders reopen, mark goes dormant but stays alive
Month 12: ladders close again after storm, mark spikes back into use, 6 likes added
Month 16: 9 likes total, no reports — too niche to attract uninformed reporters
cases.expected_signal_summary: 9 likes vs 0 reports across 16 months of episodic use
cases.human_judgment: Episodic-use technical mark with NZAC pedigree. Dormancy is not death — it is correct behaviour for a backup route.

cases.title: Pioneer Hut — La Perouse Glacier wand line (whiteout navigation)

scenario.location_desc: La Perouse Glacier between Pioneer Hut and the foot of Mt Tasman, wand line marking the safe corridor between two crevasse zones
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Saves climbers in whiteout — without wands the corridor is invisible and either edge is lethal
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Pioneer Hut
scenario.season_pattern: year-round, wands maintained by hut wardens
scenario.human_factors: Pioneer Hut warden refreshes wands at season start

events_timeline: Month 1: hut warden posts mark with photo of fresh wand line in November
Month 4: party in whiteout confirms wands are present, 'genuinely lifesaving' note added
Month 8: storm flattens half the wands, party that arrives next reports gap and replaces
Month 12: NZAC bulletin shares the mark in winter alpine notes
Month 16: 11 likes, 1 report from heli-passenger who saw glacier from above ('cant see wands')
Month 20: warden refreshes for new season, mark updated with new wand colour code
cases.expected_signal_summary: 11 likes vs 1 report, report from non-user who could not have seen wands from helicopter
cases.human_judgment: Hut-warden-maintained safety infrastructure mark. Heli-passenger report is geometrically irrelevant. Persistent.

cases.title: Centennial Hut — Fox Glacier neve fixed picket (technical supply)

scenario.location_desc: Fox Glacier neve approach to Centennial Hut, fixed snow picket left at the steep step where most parties want a top-rope belay
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Shared picket eliminates the need for every party to place gear at the same spot, reduces accumulated wear
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Centennial Hut
scenario.season_pattern: winter primary, summer the step is bare ice
scenario.human_factors: Westland guides cooperative installation

events_timeline: Month 1: Fox Glacier Guides team installs picket, posts mark with bombproof placement photo
Month 3: independent party uses picket, confirms it held two falls, adds note about snow stake angle
Month 6: NZ Mountain Guides Assoc shares in winter bulletin
Month 9: picket pulled by warming snow, party that finds it loose reposts with 'reset needed'
Month 11: Westland guides repost after re-driving picket deeper
Month 14: 7 likes, no reports, mark functions as community-asset notice
cases.expected_signal_summary: 7 likes vs 0 reports, mark functions as cooperative-asset notice
cases.human_judgment: Shared technical-asset mark, value not measured by raw engagement but by maintenance cycle. Active.

cases.title: Tasman Glacier upper neve — ski touring transition zone

scenario.location_desc: Tasman Glacier upper neve at 2000m, the transition zone between safe ski terrain and the heavily crevassed lower glacier
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks the no-ski-below-this-line GPS boundary used by NZ ski touring community
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Murchison Hut or Tasman Saddle Hut
scenario.human_factors: NZ Backcountry Skiing Association posted, refreshed annually

events_timeline: Month 1 (July): NZBSA post at start of winter season, GPS polygon for safe zone
Month 3: ski tourers confirm boundary matches actual crevasse exposure
Month 6 (Oct): season closing update, 16 likes
Month 9 (summer): mountaineer not skiing reports 'irrelevant to me' — review keeps mark
Month 12 (next winter): refreshed by same association
Month 18: 24 likes accumulated, 1 dismissive report from non-skier
Month 24: third winter season, mark a fixture in NZBSA annual bulletin
cases.expected_signal_summary: 24 likes vs 1 report from out-of-context reporter
cases.human_judgment: Activity-specific safety mark. Non-skier report is out of scope. Mark serves a defined audience well.

cases.title: Mueller Glacier entry — moraine collapse zone (current hazard)

scenario.location_desc: Mueller Glacier lateral moraine at the entry to the glacier proper, the collapsing moraine wall that dropped 50m in 2022 storms
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks active collapse zone where standing on the lip risks 50m fall onto glacier ice
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Mueller Hut
scenario.season_pattern: year-round, worse after rain or freeze-thaw
scenario.human_factors: DOC ranger plus geological survey co-author

events_timeline: Month 1: GNS Science geologist drops mark after annual moraine survey, links instability report
Month 4: DOC ranger adds confirmation, photo of new collapse scarp
Month 7: party witnesses small collapse from safe distance, adds video evidence
Month 10: tourist reports 'the moraine has been there for centuries, mark is alarmist'
Month 13: another large collapse documented by Mueller Hut warden
Month 16: 19 likes, 2 reports
Month 18: GNS publishes paper citing this exact location, mark gains scientific citation
cases.expected_signal_summary: 19 likes vs 2 reports, scientific paper as backing evidence
cases.human_judgment: GNS-backed geomorphic hazard mark. Tourist intuition does not override published science. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Cook Village — Aoraki summit weather window radio relay

scenario.location_desc: Plateau Hut weather window radio relay schedule, mark documents the 6am and 6pm radio sched for summit-bound parties
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Lets parties at Plateau Hut catch reliable weather updates from MetService aviation forecast via Mt Cook Village base
scenario.season_pattern: summer summit season Nov-March primary use
scenario.human_factors: Mt Cook Village SAR base maintains schedule

events_timeline: Month 1: SAR base posts the schedule with frequencies
Month 3: party uses sched to abort summit ahead of front, credits mark
Month 6: schedule changes, SAR updates mark with new times
Month 9: 14 likes from summit logbook climbers
Month 12: hut warden adds note about radio battery cache location
Month 16: 21 likes, 0 reports
Month 22: schedule refreshed for new season
cases.expected_signal_summary: 21 likes vs 0 reports, SAR-maintained operational data
cases.human_judgment: Operational radio infrastructure mark. SAR-authored, life-saving in weather decisions. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Aspiring SW Ridge — ridge gendarme rappel station

scenario.location_desc: Mt Aspiring SW Ridge mid-ridge gendarme, fixed double-bolt rappel station to bypass an exposed step on the standard descent
scenario.intrinsic_quality: 30m rappel anchor that saves down-climbing a 5.6 step in mountaineering boots
scenario.human_factors: rebolted by Aspiring Guides 2023, confirmed by ASCA bolting standards

events_timeline: Month 1: Aspiring Guides team rebolts, posts with hardware specs (12mm glue-in)
Month 4: independent party uses rappel, confirms anchor, adds note on rope drag
Month 7: NZAC bulletin includes mark in standard route description
Month 10: 11 likes from named summit logbook climbers
Month 13: rope-test party confirms anchor still bombproof after 2 winters
Month 16: 14 likes, 0 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 14 likes vs 0 reports, ASCA-standard hardware
cases.human_judgment: Standard rappel station mark. Hardware spec and ASCA compliance make this a reference, not an opinion.

cases.title: Mt Sefton — Footstool basin avalanche debris field bivvy site

scenario.location_desc: Footstool basin under Mt Sefton, an emergency bivvy site in the lee of an avalanche-debris boulder used by parties caught out late
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks a survivable bivvy spot if descent is not possible by nightfall, sheltered from west wind
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Mueller Hut
scenario.human_factors: posted after 2022 SAR incident where party survived overnight here

events_timeline: Month 1: SAR posts after debrief of party who used the spot to survive a storm
Month 4: NZAC mountain skills instructor adds the location to syllabus mark list
Month 8: 6 likes from instructors and one party who used it preventively
Month 12: party posts photo confirming the boulder is still there post-winter
Month 15: 9 likes total, no reports
Month 18: SAR refreshes after annual review
cases.expected_signal_summary: 9 likes vs 0 reports, low-volume but high-consequence
cases.human_judgment: Emergency bivvy mark — low engagement reflects rare use, not low quality. SAR-authored. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Tasman — Marcel Couloir cornice break detection

scenario.location_desc: Marcel Couloir on Mt Tasman, the cornice at the top of the couloir that breaks predictably after warm afternoons
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Marks the cornice with windward GPS line so climbers know when they are in fall zone
scenario.human_factors: NZAC ice climbing community

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC ice climber posts after near-miss, photo of broken cornice debris
Month 4: second party confirms approximate cornice line
Month 8: cornice breaks while party watches from below, mark validated visually
Month 12: 7 likes from named ice climbers
Month 15: solo climber adds note about morning temperature threshold for breakage
Month 20: 10 likes, 0 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 10 likes vs 0 reports, community-curated cornice intel
cases.human_judgment: Specialist hazard mark for ice climbers. Tiny audience, no contention. Persistent.

cases.title: Aoraki — Anzac Peaks traverse, technical chimney pitch

scenario.location_desc: Anzac Peaks traverse on Aoraki, a hidden chimney pitch on the mid-traverse that is invisible until you are 5m from it
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Without mark, parties spend up to an hour searching for the entry, in a no-stop zone
scenario.human_factors: extreme niche, only top-tier guided ascents

events_timeline: Month 1: senior IFMGA guide posts after multi-decade familiarity with route
Month 6: another guide confirms with photo from chimney mouth
Month 12: 4 likes total, but every like from named summit log climber
Month 18: NZAC traversers thank guide directly
Month 24: 6 likes, 0 reports — the audience is 20 people in NZ
cases.expected_signal_summary: 6 likes vs 0 reports across 24 months
cases.human_judgment: Tiniest possible audience, highest-skill mark. Engagement is irrelevant — survival of the mark depends on community trust, which is total here.

cases.title: Mt Earnslaw — west peak NW ridge variant snow stake bivvy gear cache

scenario.location_desc: Mt Earnslaw west peak NW ridge, gear cache at 2400m platform with shared snow stakes and a pulk for emergency descent
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Cooperative gear cache maintained by Glenorchy alpine community, reduces solo party risk
scenario.signal: no signal, syncs at Earnslaw Burn campsite
scenario.human_factors: Glenorchy alpine club cooperative

events_timeline: Month 1: Glenorchy alpine club posts cache location after annual restock
Month 4: party uses cache after broken crampon, returns replacement gear
Month 8: 4 likes, all from confirmed users who left replacement gear
Month 12: cache audited, all gear present, mark refreshed
Month 16: 6 likes, 0 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 6 likes vs 0 reports, cooperative cache with audit cycle
cases.human_judgment: Community-cooperative cache, audit-validated. Engagement reflects cache use, not popularity contest.

cases.title: Mt Sefton — Footstool ridge lightning rod hazard zone

scenario.location_desc: Mt Sefton Footstool ridge crest at 2300m, exposed metal anchor that has been struck by lightning twice and acts as electrical attractor in storms
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Names a no-go-during-electrical-activity zone, advises 100m descent if storm approaches
scenario.human_factors: MetService alpine forecaster collaborated

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC member posts after watching strike during 2024 storm
Month 3: MetService forecaster confirms electrical exposure of ridge
Month 6: party retreats correctly, credits mark with avoiding strike
Month 9: 11 likes, including from MetService alpine team
Month 12: another strike documented at same anchor
Month 14: 14 likes, 0 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 14 likes vs 0 reports, two strike events documented during mark life
cases.human_judgment: Lightning hazard mark with MetService backing and witnessed strike events. Permanent through storm season cycles.

cases.title: Mt Aspiring — Bonar Glacier sastrugi false trail

scenario.location_desc: Bonar Glacier between French Ridge Hut and Quarterdeck, a sastrugi pattern that looks like an obvious party-trail leading northeast but actually goes into crevasse zone
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Anti-mark warning that the false trail is a wind feature, real route is 50m south
scenario.season_pattern: spring after wind events most deceptive
scenario.human_factors: posted after near-miss by NZAC training course

events_timeline: Month 1: NZAC instructor posts after course participant followed false trail and roped party caught the slip
Month 4: party in flat light confirms the trap is real, adds photo of both lines side by side
Month 8: hut warden refreshes after spring storm
Month 12: 16 likes, including from instructor consortium
Month 16: tourist reports 'I followed the obvious tracks and was fine' — but tourist had clear weather
Month 20: 22 likes vs 1 report
cases.expected_signal_summary: 22 likes vs 1 report, condition-dependent hazard
cases.human_judgment: Anti-pattern hazard mark — danger only manifests in flat light. Clear-weather report does not invalidate. Permanent.

cases.title: Mueller Hut Route — water source midway, tarn behind moraine

scenario.location_desc: Mueller Hut Route midway up, hidden tarn 30m off-track behind a moraine fold, drinkable in summer when hut tank is low
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Critical in summer when 200+ visitors per day deplete hut water tank by afternoon
scenario.human_factors: hut warden posted, used by overflow trampers

events_timeline: Month 1: warden posts during peak season after hut runs dry
Month 2: 30 likes within 2 weeks from same-week visitors
Month 5 (winter): tarn frozen, mark gets seasonal-only flag
Month 8 (summer): mark reactivates, 22 more likes
Month 12: 60 likes, 2 reports from people who couldn't find it
Month 14: warden adds bearing-from-track instructions
Month 18: 78 likes vs 3 reports
cases.expected_signal_summary: 78 likes vs 3 reports, all reports from people who didn't follow bearing
cases.human_judgment: Seasonal-active supply mark from hut warden. Reports reflect difficulty finding without bearing, not falsehood. Persistent.

cases.title: Ball Pass — Caroline Hut access, river crossing bypass route

scenario.location_desc: Ball Pass approach to Caroline Hut, a moraine bypass to avoid a chest-deep glacial-fed river crossing in melt season
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Adds 40 minutes but eliminates a non-trivial drowning risk on the standard approach
scenario.season_pattern: critical in summer melt, less needed in winter freeze
scenario.human_factors: Caroline Hut warden plus DOC backcountry team

events_timeline: Month 1 (Dec): warden posts during peak melt season
Month 4: party that bypassed credits mark, photo of unbypassed river chest-deep
Month 7 (winter): river frozen, mark less relevant, but stays alive with seasonal note
Month 11 (next summer): refreshed
Month 14: a Land SAR rescue happens at the unbypassed crossing, mark validated
Month 18: 17 likes, 1 report from winter user who didnt need it
Month 22: 24 likes vs 1 report
cases.expected_signal_summary: 24 likes vs 1 report, validated by SAR rescue at the bypassed crossing
cases.human_judgment: Seasonal alpine bypass with SAR-incident validation. Winter report is out of season scope. Permanent.

cases.title: Cascade Saddle — emergency shelter rock overhang midway

scenario.location_desc: Cascade Saddle midway between Pylon and Dart Hut, a rock overhang that fits 4 people standing, used as last-resort lightning shelter
scenario.intrinsic_quality: Only viable shelter on the most exposed section of NZs deadliest tramping route
scenario.season_pattern: year-round, summer thunderstorm and winter wind
scenario.human_factors: DOC and a survivor of 2018 storm-rescue co-authored

events_timeline: Month 1: 2018 incident survivor posts mark with photo of the overhang
Month 3: DOC ranger validates and adds it to safety briefing
Month 6: party uses overhang during thunderstorm, posts thanks
Month 10: 19 likes, 0 reports
Month 14: another party uses during whiteout, mark gains 'all-conditions shelter' tag
Month 17: tourist reports 'doesnt look like much of a shelter' — but they were in clear weather
Month 20: 26 likes vs 1 report
cases.expected_signal_summary: 26 likes vs 1 report, multiple use-case validations
cases.human_judgment: Last-resort shelter on highest-exposure route. Aesthetic complaint is irrelevant to function. Permanent.

cases.title: Mt Cook Range — Sealy Range traverse, false col navigation trap

scenario.location_desc: Sealy Range traverse near Mt Annette, a false col that draws parties off-route into a 200m drop above bluffs
